notes: Batch 2026-W47 (harvests read: 2026-11-10 (232 items), 2026-11-11 (627 items, the first run with the 44 new sources) and 2026-11-16 (451 items; the scheduled Monday run never fired, so the review dispatched it by hand at 14:13 UTC). Eleven posts, every photo viewed on the preview sheets (three preview rounds, 51 sets, 541 photos). Held picks released: Bistrot a Franky (0039), Echo (0040). New: 0029 The Penrose Room (classic, 1961, Tihany restoration), 0030 The Fifth Avenue Hotel (Joe Thomas), 0031 Theodora (Home Studios, Brian W. Ferry), 0032 Hotel Kinsley (Studio Robert McKinley, 2019), 0033 Bar Moruno (Studio UNLTD, 2022), 0034 Hotel Saint Augustine (Julie Soefer), 0035 Uchiko Miami (Islyn, William Jess Laird), 0037 Hotel Regina Biarritz (classic, 1906, Chzon), 0038 Hotel du Couvent (Festen). Index 0036 was reserved for the Arizona Inn (Carol M. Highsmith, 2018, seven frames) and withdrawn: its masters are 227 to 303 MB TIFFs and tile.loc.gov answered 429 after the first one in the preview run; the IIIF derivatives 404 for these items. It stays on archive_targets.json for a week when loc.gov cooperates; 0036 is not reused. Dropped after viewing: Alex Staniloff pages (Hoexters, Crane Club, Chambers, Lambs Club, Santi: food and portraits, one or two rooms each), Hotel Clermont (posed models in most frames, three rooms), Elsa (Home Studios conflict, 2017), Scott's London and Mr C and Nubeluz (one MBDS post per batch), The Breakers and Daniel (one Tihany post), Bavel and Rose Mary (one UNLTD post), Public and Ryder (one Joe Thomas post), Hotel Kinsley main page (guest rooms), Silver Lake Pool & Inn and Helms Bakery and Oiji Mi and Quality Bistro and Providence and Hogshead (under the size gate), Ditto (AD, every frame fails compression), Peak and Avenue at The Edge (courtesy Tao Group, very clean symmetrical frames, possible render; held back), Jeune et Jolie (three distinct views), El Condor (food only), Rochechouart (Festen conflict). Watch list: Focacha READY was two frames of the same view plus two; Sisters READY still carries other projects' photos.

card: BUREAU OF LEISURE NO. 0029
THE PENROSE ROOM. THE BROADMOOR, COLORADO SPRINGS.
OPENED IN 1961 ATOP THE NEW SOUTH TOWER.
THE RESORT WAS FOUNDED IN 1918 BY SPENCER PENROSE.
REIMAGINED BY TIHANY DESIGN. REOPENED IN 2025.
A LOUNGE LIKE A WESTERN SALOON. THREE DINING ROOMS.
IN A WORD: DEBONAIR.
posts.alt_hint: A wood-panelled hotel dining room with teal floral carpet, curved banquettes, brass picture lights and tall windows onto the mountains.
posts.bring: BRING WHOEVER STILL OWNS A BLAZER.
posts.facts_from: Tihany Design project page (1918 founding, saloon lounge, three dining rooms, photo Amaury Laparra); The Gazette 2026-04-22 (opened 1961, ninth floor of the South Tower) and 2025-08-13 (reopened, taking reservations). Classic: open since 1961, current photographs.
posts.photo_note: 2026-11-16 second pass: the first build benched the set (slides do not match: the bar counter and coral banquette frames were far warmer than the green room). Now four frames of close tone: green dining room, bar with zebra stools, main dining room, red-lamp dining corner.

card: BUREAU OF LEISURE NO. 0030
THE FIFTH AVENUE HOTEL. NOMAD, NEW YORK.
A LANDMARKED MCKIM, MEAD & WHITE MANSION.
153 ROOMS. INTERIORS BY MARTIN BRUDNIZKI.
CAFE CARMELLINI BY CHEF ANDREW CARMELLINI.
OPENED IN 2023 BY FLANEUR HOSPITALITY.
IN A WORD: PLUSH.
posts.alt_hint: A hotel restaurant with a tree growing through it, tiered chandeliers of glass globes, blue velvet banquettes and tan leather chairs at white-clothed tables.
posts.bring: BRING SOMEONE WHO ASKS WHO DID THE INTERIORS.
posts.facts_from: Hospitality Net announcement (NoMad, 28th Street, landmarked McKim Mead & White mansion, 153 rooms, Martin Brudnizki, Cafe Carmellini by Andrew Carmellini, Flaneur Hospitality, opening fall 2023). Public rooms only: restaurant, bar, fireplace lounge, library, corridor; the green suite frames were left out (no bedrooms).

card: BUREAU OF LEISURE NO. 0031
THEODORA. FORT GREENE, BROOKLYN.
FROM CHEF TOMER BLECHMAN OF MISS ADA.
AGED PLASTER, ZELLIGE TILE, CEPPO DI GRÈ SHELVES.
SEVENTY-SIX SEATS IN THE DINING ROOM.
INTERIOR ARCHITECTURE BY HOME STUDIOS, 2023.
IN A WORD: TERRAZZO.
posts.alt_hint: A plaster-walled restaurant with a long pale bar, rush-seated stools, a barrel-vaulted ceiling and a wood-fired kitchen behind.
posts.facts_from: Home Studios project page (Brooklyn 2023, photographs by Brian W. Ferry); Wallpaper 2024-02-08 (Tomer Blechman of Miss Ada, aged plaster, zellige, ceppo di gre shelves, 76 seats, terrazzo-look tile floor).

card: BUREAU OF LEISURE NO. 0032
HOTEL KINSLEY. UPTOWN STOCKADE, KINGSTON, NEW YORK.
FOUR HISTORIC BUILDINGS IN THE HUDSON VALLEY.
THE MAIN HOUSE IS A FORMER BANK ON WALL STREET.
CHECK IN HAPPENS INSIDE THE OLD VAULT.
INTERIORS BY STUDIO ROBERT MCKINLEY, 2019.
IN A WORD: TWEEDY.
posts.alt_hint: A hotel restaurant with an oak bar, blue-cushioned stools, rust velvet booths, Persian rugs and tall windows, and the old bank vault door at check-in.
posts.facts_from: Dezeen 2019-08-31 (four 17th to 19th century buildings in the Uptown Stockade District, 301 Wall Street a former bank, check-in in the vault, restaurant and bar; photography Nicole Franzen). Photos: six from the studio's restaurant page plus the vault frame from its hotel page (same project, same shoot); the hotel page is otherwise guest rooms. CREDIT TO CONFIRM: the studio pages name no photographer; Nicole Franzen is Dezeen's credit for the same images.

card: BUREAU OF LEISURE NO. 0033
BAR MORUNO. SILVER LAKE, LOS ANGELES.
RED DOUBLE DOORS ONTO SUNSET BOULEVARD.
BOOTHS OF SLATTED WALNUT IN PAPRIKA.
OLIVE GREEN BACK BAR. TURMERIC GOLD BANQUETTE.
1,700 SQUARE FEET. STUDIO UNLTD, 2022.
IN A WORD: LOUCHE.
posts.alt_hint: A long Spanish-style bar room with a green back bar, olive velvet stools, walnut booths in paprika and a yellow banquette under framed posters.
posts.bring: BRING WHOEVER'S "ONE DRINK" IS NEVER ONE.
posts.facts_from: Studio UNLTD project page (all card facts). No photographer named on the page or in Hospitality Design's July 2022 piece: credit left empty, caption ends DM for credit.
posts.photo_note: 2026-11-16: benched on first build (private room and yellow banquette are much warmer than the bar frames, and the banquette frame is over the saturation limit). Only three frames of matching tone exist on the page, so it stays benched and goes to the watch list.

card: BUREAU OF LEISURE NO. 0034
HOTEL SAINT AUGUSTINE. MONTROSE, HOUSTON.
BUNKHOUSE'S FIRST HOUSTON HOTEL. 71 ROOMS.
FIVE SMALL BUILDINGS BY LAKE FLATO.
INTERIORS BY POST COMPANY. DEEP BLUE LOBBY AND BAR.
A BURLED WALNUT DESK. A ROUND HEATED POOL.
IN A WORD: GROOVY.
posts.alt_hint: A dark-blue hotel lounge with a red curved sofa, chrome-framed chairs, burl wood walls, sheer linen curtains and a long dining table under gilt mirrors.
posts.facts_from: Hospitality Design 2025-03-13 (Montrose, 71 rooms across five small buildings, Lake Flato, Post Company with Bunkhouse, deep blue lobby and bar, burled walnut reception desk, circular heated pool); Hospitality Net (Bunkhouse's first Houston concept). Frames: bar, lounge, chrome chairs, red shelving wall, courtyard; bedrooms left out.
posts.photo_note: 2026-11-16 second pass: first build benched the set (the courtyard and the red shelving wall sat outside the tone spread). Now: lounge and restaurant wide (cover), bar, front door, green bathroom with corridor, chrome-chair lounge, green tiled bathroom; the build may drop one or two of the last three. Third pass: the second build kept the lounge, the front door and two bathrooms, which is not a set to be in; now exactly four frames (lounge, bar, chrome-chair lounge, front door). If their tone does not match, it benches rather than builds a weak post.

posts.reminds: a Lina Bo Bardi beach house
card: BUREAU OF LEISURE NO. 0035
UCHIKO MIAMI. SUNSET HARBOUR, MIAMI BEACH.
TROPICAL BRUTALISM MEETS JAPANESE DECO.
A GLOWING BAR BUILT FROM GLASS BLOCKS.
TEAK SHUTTERS, CONCRETE, SEA GREEN MARBLE MOSAICS.
A HOST STAND LIKE A THATCHED ROOF. ISLYN, 2025.
IN A WORD: LACQUERED.
posts.alt_hint: A dim Japanese restaurant with a sushi counter of blue tile, walnut booths, fringed lanterns and palms behind louvred teak shutters.
posts.facts_from: Islyn Studio project page (tropical brutalism and Japanese deco, marina-side, glass block bar, teak shutters, exposed concrete, sea green marble mosaics, thatched-roof host stand, 2025, partner William Jess Laird); Dezeen 2025-08-23 via 10minhotel mirror (Sunset Harbor, photography William Jess Laird). Uchiko is a Hai Hospitality brand; this location is a single Islyn design piece.

card: BUREAU OF LEISURE NO. 0037
HOTEL REGINA. AVENUE DE L'IMPERATRICE, BIARRITZ.
BUILT AS A HOTEL IN 1906 BY HENRY MARTINET.
A FIFTEEN-METRE-HIGH BELLE EPOQUE ATRIUM.
EILEEN GRAY STOOLS. ART DECO TILES BY WINCKELMANS.
REDONE BY DOROTHEE MEILICHZON, 2023.
IN A WORD: STARCHED.
posts.alt_hint: A white Belle Epoque atrium three storeys high, with striped sofas, terracotta armchairs, rope lamps and a glass roof.
posts.facts_from: Studio Chzon project page (all card facts; Photos: Patrick Locqueneux; July 2023). Classic: hotel since 1906, current photographs. Four frames (atrium from the gallery, atrium seating, restaurant corner, red-arched corridor); the suite and dressing-room frames were left out.

card: BUREAU OF LEISURE NO. 0038
HOTEL DU COUVENT. OLD TOWN, NICE.
BUILT IN 1604 FOR THE ORDER OF SAINT CLARE.
A DECADE OF RESTORATION LED BY VALERY GREGO.
EIGHTY-EIGHT ROOMS. INTERIORS BY FESTEN.
ROMAN-STYLE BATHS. GARDENS OF 300 PLANT SPECIES.
IN A WORD: SUNLIT.
posts.alt_hint: A lime-plastered salon in a former convent, with linen sofas, a terracotta floor, paper globe lamps and an arched loggia onto the garden.
posts.facts_from: Festen project page (17th century convent, Nice); Yatzer 2024-11-26 (built 1604 by the Order of Saint Clare, decade-long restoration led by Valery Grego's Perseus, 88 rooms, Roman-inspired baths, 2.5 acres with over 300 plant species, Festen interiors). Festen's page names no photographer: credit left empty.

card: BUREAU OF LEISURE NO. 0039
BISTROT À FRANKY. MILE END, MONTREAL.
CHEF FRANCIS BLAIS. ATELIER ZÉBULON PERRON.
A ZINC BAR UNDER A MILLED ALUMINIUM WINE CELLAR.
PYREX TUBE CHANDELIERS BY LAMBERT & FILS.
ART ON THE WALLS CURATED BY XAVIER DOLAN.

posts.alt_hint: A monochrome white bistro with a zinc bar, blond leather banquettes under big mirrors, butcher block tables and glowing tube chandeliers.
posts.facts_from: Dezeen 2026-10-30 (full text in the 2026-11-10 harvest): Mile End, chef Francis Blais, monochrome whites and beiges, zinc bar top, milled aluminium wine cellar with portholes, Pyrex tube chandeliers by Lambert & Fils, art curated by Xavier Dolan; photography by Alex Lesage. Photos viewed 2026-11-09 (held.json).

card: BUREAU OF LEISURE NO. 0040
ECHO. GROOT HANDELSGEBOUW, ROTTERDAM.
A LISTENING BAR IN A POST-WAR OFFICE BLOCK.
A BAR BUILT FROM WOODEN SHIPPING CRATES.
OMBRÉ MIRRORS AND A RESIN LAMP BY SABINE MARCELIS.
INTERIOR BY CLOUD. OPENED SEPTEMBER 2026.
IN A WORD: SMOKY.
posts.alt_hint: A concrete-walled listening bar with a crate-built counter, speaker towers, modular vinyl shelving and a sofa under an orange light.
posts.bring: BRING SOMEONE WHO HAS BEEN TO JAPAN. TWICE.
posts.facts_from: Dezeen 2026-10-30 (full text in the 2026-11-10 harvest): ground floor of Groot Handelsgebouw, a post-war office block; bar built with Barendregt's Kistenfabriek from shipping crates; Sabine Marcelis ombre mirrors and resin lamp; interior by Paul Cournet's studio Cloud; open since early September; photography by Sophia van den Hoek. Photos viewed 2026-11-09 (held.json). BRING line: CONDITIONAL listening bars.
